content.text:
Both objects exist and the rule is enabled.

**Data view findings:** `kibana_sample_data_logs` has 14,074 requests from 1,001 client IPs across 448 URLs, spanning 2026-10-04 to 2026-12-03. Response codes are 200 (12,832), 404 (801) and 503 (441). The only 5xx code is 503. Key fields are `@timestamp`, `clientip`, `bytes`, `url.keyword`, and `response.keyword`.

**Dashboard:** "EFF-9d6ec98e Web logs overview" (`eff-9d6ec98e-web-logs-overview-93c596158c5a`) has six panels:
- Total requests (metric)
- Unique client IPs (metric)
- Average response bytes (metric)
- Requests over time (line, date histogram)
- Requests by response code (pie)
- Top URLs by requests (bar)

I set the dashboard's time range to 2026-10-01 through 2026-12-31 so the sample data shows up. The default last-7-days range would show nothing.

**Alert rule:** "EFF-9d6ec98e 5xx spike" (`c399c64d-2edb-49fb-be75-e2284b8b87e1`) is enabled, runs every 1m, and fires when the count of requests with `response.keyword` matching `5??` in the last 5 minutes is greater than 10. I checked the match condition separately and it finds all 441 of the 503 responses.

The rule's status is "pending" because the sample data's timestamps are in October–December 2026, not near the current time. The rule will likely not fire unless new 5xx events arrive in the window. Also, the Kibana sample data is static, so the rule will not fire from it on its own.
